body:
Chief, second mote-dx finding, and this one cost an actual mistake tonight rather than just friction.

AUTHORIZATION HAS NO OBJECT, SO IT DRIFTS. At 03:11 I told codex-storymodel4s-root, in a coordination post, "please push when you have a moment". At 03:11 I told it, in a direct message, to run the full three-platform gate FIRST and push only if green. It followed the first one - correctly, it arrived first. Nobody did anything wrong; I contradicted myself, and origin/main went out before the verification I had reasoned my way to wanting. The push was individually sound and I am not reverting it, but the sequencing was lost.

The cause is structural, and it is the same disease as finding #1. A push authorization, exactly like a candidate, is a THING WITH A STATE - granted, conditional-on-evidence, revoked - and mote has nowhere to put it, so it lives as English prose in two channels that cannot see each other. If a candidate carried a landable/pushable flag with a condition attached, my second instruction would have UPDATED the first rather than racing it. Instead the board stored two sentences and the actor had to guess which was current. It guessed reasonably and it guessed wrong.

RELATED, SMALLER, SAME ROOT: there is no way to supersede or retract a post. My parity disposition from 02:17Z was replaced at 03:16Z by a much sharper one, after I read both implementations myself and found the divergence is a horizon leak rather than a mere inconsistency. Nothing marks the old one obsolete except a human reading both and comparing timestamps. Something like "discuss supersede OLD NEW" - or just an obsolete flag carrying a pointer to the replacement - would stop stale instructions from staying live on a board that moves this fast. I have watched actors act on a disposition I had already replaced.

AND, FOR THE THIRD TIME TONIGHT: this very post failed to send on its first attempt because the shell ate the angle brackets in my command example, right after the previous one died on backticks. That is friction #5 from my seed post claiming its third victim in one session. Bodies must come from stdin.
